title: Finite-projective Hom-complex scalar extension
statement: Let A,B be commutative rings and phi:A -> B a ring homomorphism. Use the one-object ringed-site categories and normalized extension data d of [def-pc-perfect-rhom-base-change-map], including its pure-tensor equation on every Hom-complex product projection. Let P,Q be cochain complexes of A-module sheaves, with P bounded and with finite projective terms evaluated at the unique object. Then the chain map d.homMap(P,Q): B tensor_A Hom_A^\bullet(P,Q) -> Hom_B^\bullet(B tensor_A P,B tensor_A Q) is an isomorphism. No K-flatness of Q or flatness of B over A is assumed.

source.place: Lemma 0A6A, lemma-base-change-RHom, clause (1); bounded finite-projective representative argument

proof.text: For each degree n and index p, apply finiteProjectiveRingHom_extension_exists to M=P.X p and N=Q.X(p+n), using hp p and hf p. This supplies the normalized termwise isomorphisms required by the finite-product assembly theorem.

Apply boundedRingHom_extension_degree_isIso in degree n to F=d.extension and t=(d.homMap P Q).f n. Supply d.objects, d.additive, the given support bound hb, the termwise comparisons from the preceding step, and exactly d.homMap_pure P Q n as the normalization hypothesis.

The previous step gives IsIso for every degree component. Apply Mathlib HomologicalComplex.Hom.isIso_of_components to the already constructed chain map d.homMap P Q. No additional differential compatibility needs to be proved.
